set.title: Formal requirements are checked by machine
set.content:
Backup · Development · nr-llm v0.43.19

  1. Define the schema Define required fields, data types, permitted values and lengths.
  2. Generate the answer The application passes the schema to completeStructured().
  3. Check locally nr-llm checks the answer against the supported schema.
  4. Only on errors One repair attempt; then a valid result or an error.

A valid format does not yet prove a correct statement.

Test example: permitted status values and at most 160 characters for the description.

Executed test example · How it works and source evidence

Original slide 39

set.title: How does nr-llm check faithfulness to the source?
set.content:
Backup · nr-llm 0.43.19 · checked on 6 Nov 2026

  1. The application supplies Request, finished draft and original sources; plus concrete test questions.
  2. nr-llm assesses The DecisionService has a model assess the criteria and returns a structured result.
  3. The application decides Thresholds, revision and human approval remain part of the workflow.

Available as a general service since 0.39. A check result is not proof of truth either.

Example: “Is 4 November supported by the source?” This assessment was not run in the schema example.

DecisionService and integration

Original slide 56

set.title: What can term lists check?
set.content:
Backup · Quality · nr-llm 0.43.19

Define the scope
Assign lists to the desired configurations. Without an assignment this list does not check the call.

Match terms
Blocked terms must not occur. Required terms must be contained in suitable text answers.

Stop the output
A violation blocks the checked output. In an agent run, an affected write call is neither offered nor executed.

Limit: paraphrases are not detected. In an agent run, write arguments are checked; chat text and required words are excluded.

Example: “Rabatt*” also matches “Rabattaktion”. Required words do not apply to short texts under 30 words or to JSON.

Term lists and exceptions

Original slide 60

set.title: Skills are included as prompt context
set.content:
Backup · Development · nr-llm v0.43.19

  1. Load the source Maintain the skill in the backend or sync it from GitHub; pin the version.
  2. Approve the content Check version and origin; approve the skills you want.
  3. Assign to the task Assign skills, or load approved skills when needed.
  4. Insert the text Approved + trusted: system message. Unreviewed always-skills: user context.

Skill text supplies context. Associated scripts and files are neither executed nor loaded.

Skills assigned on demand need approval; process skills need an explicit call.

How it works and source evidence

Original slide 41

set.title: How does your own extension integrate nr-llm?
set.content:
Developer questions · nr-llm v0.43.19

  1. Inject the service Use the matching nr-llm interface via TYPO3 dependency injection.
  2. Prepare the call Determine inputs, permissions and the desired configuration.
  3. Request the result A direct feature service or a recurring task with a prompt template.
  4. Process the result Handle errors, check the output and implement the business approval.

nr-llm takes care of the model connection. The extension designs the business workflow.

Example: completeForConfiguration($prompt, $configuration) returns a CompletionResponse.

Interfaces and source evidence

Original slide 44

set.title: Where do context and knowledge come from?
set.content:
Developer questions · nr-llm v0.43.19

Passed in
Prompt, current content and skill texts come from the application.

Looked up
Search tools return excerpts with sources from existing TYPO3 searches.

Maintained separately
Index updates and persistent vector search remain separate integration tasks.

The model sees sources that were provided or retrieved – no automatic body of knowledge.

Interfaces and source evidence

Original slide 45

set.title: Switching models needs a suitability test
set.content:
Backup · Integration · nr-llm v0.43.19

Switch the connection
The application uses a named configuration. Model and provider can be changed behind it.

Check suitability
Check required capabilities, context size and parameters; re-test typical tasks.

Try out the fallback
Test fallback configurations for outages. Check the data destination, quality and cost of every fallback.

A shared interface does not make models interchangeable on the merits.

Model choice and capabilities · Fallback in the source code

Original slide 47

set.title: Which foundations exist for your own knowledge search?
set.content:
Backup · Development · Search and RAG infrastructure

EXT:index
Indexing framework for TYPO3 content: preparation and hand-over via events or webhooks.

SEAL + seal_ai
Search abstraction, embeddings and vector store; optional read-only MCP search access. seal_ai: proof of concept.

smart_search
Services for vectors, semantic search and RAG in your own extensions. Marked as alpha.

These building blocks take care of knowledge access. An AI layer on its own does not maintain a search index.

Indexing framework · SEAL / Symfony AI · RAG building blocks

Original slide 55

set.title: How do applications use source checking?
set.content:
Backup · nr-llm 0.43.19 · checked on 6 Nov 2026

AI Search
An anti-hallucination check is documented. Which nr-llm service it calls internally is not verified here.

Repurpose: checkpoints
PR 205: check the briefing against the original. Then compare every finished format text against the original again.

Repurpose: workflow
Check after shortening, before audio and media production. Keep automatic assessment separate from editorial approval.

“Not checked” and “check failed” must not look like a passed result.

The released Repurpose 0.14.0 lacks the semantic source comparison. PR 205 implements it but has not yet been merged or released.

Repurpose 0.14.0 · reviewed state · PR 205 · implementation

Original slide 59

set.title: MCP connects the agent with tools
set.content:
Backup · Integration · nr-llm v0.43.19

  1. The model proposes Chooses an offered tool and formulates its arguments.
  2. nr-llm checks Backend administrators only; additional permissions and approvals limit the call.
  3. The MCP client calls Sends the tool call via HTTP to the external server.
  4. The result flows back Text result or error becomes context for the next model step.

In this workflow TYPO3 is the MCP client. The external server executes the tool.

Beforehand: configure the server, import the tool catalogue and enable individual tools.

How it works and source evidence

Original slide 42

set.title: What happens with errors or excess context?
set.content:
Developer questions · nr-llm v0.43.19

Connection disrupted
Retry a limited number of times; depending on the error, use a configured fallback connection.

Access wrong
Correct authentication and configuration; report the error to the application.

Context too large
Old chat rounds can be dropped. The application has to split a single prompt appropriately.

The application needs an error path; retries and fallback do not solve every problem.

Interfaces and source evidence

Original slide 46

set.title: What happens when a provider fails?
set.content:
Backup · Effort and operations · nr-llm 0.43.19

Error pause
The circuit breaker counts suitable provider errors. After the configured threshold, further calls abort quickly for a while.

Fallback path
A configured fallback tries another target on connection errors, overload, server errors or an open circuit breaker.

Check recovery
After the pause, one probe call is allowed. Success closes the block; another error opens it again.

Limit: no availability guarantee. Authentication and configuration errors do not trigger an automatic fallback.

Default: a 30-second pause after five matching errors. Fallback targets have to be set up.

Circuit breaker and fallback · Defaults

Original slide 61

set.title: Which data may go to which provider?
set.content:
Backup · nr-llm 0.43.19 · checked on 6 Nov 2026

Data classGlobal externalEU externalPrivately hostedLocal
Public contentYesYesYesYes
Editorial contentYesYesYesYes
Source codeNoYesYesYes
Internal configurationNoYesYesYes
Operational data / logsNoNoYesYes
Credential-related dataNoNoNoYes

The model name does not determine the zone. Local open-source code is classified the same way as confidential project code.

Fixed policy: read_source and search_code belong to the class sourceCode. With externalGlobal + enforce they are blocked even for admins.

Zones and assignment · Tool classes

Original slide 57

set.title: Where are the limits of the data check?
set.content:
Backup · nr-llm 0.43.19 · checked on 6 Nov 2026

Declaration
Free text is not classified automatically. Wrong information about data class or provider zone is not detected from the content.

Tools
The tool's own declaration takes precedence over the group class; otherwise the strictest class applies. MCP takes over the server class and enforces it even in observe mode.

Actual destination
Fallbacks count too. With dynamic model selection, some call paths can choose separately for checking and sending.

No MCP import without a valid data class. The policy detects neither sensitive content nor the actual data location.

Paths with a passed ModelResolution, including the DecisionService, bind checking and sending to the same resolution.

Dynamic model selection · MCP classification

Original slide 58

set.title: How are credentials protected?
set.content:
Backup · Data and requirements · nr-llm 0.43.19

Store in the vault
Configured API credentials point to a secret in nr-vault. The configuration contains its identifier.

Insert at call time
The secure HTTP client inserts the credential for the service call. The key does not belong in the model instruction.

Mask text
nr-llm replaces recognisable secret patterns in prompt, response and thinking. This masking is mandatory.

Limit: only known patterns are detected. Tool arguments and embeddings are excluded; personal data is not detected in general.

Example: store the API key as a vault reference instead of copying it into the system prompt.

Credentials via nr-vault · Masking and limits

Original slide 62

set.title: How does the agent read external web pages?
set.content:
Backup · Data and requirements · nr-llm 0.43.19

Enable deliberately
The web tool is switched off initially. Once enabled, a call requires human consent by default.

Check the address
The start address and every redirect go through the address check. Private target addresses are rejected even when the host is allowed.

Limit the text
The tool returns limited text and marks it as untrusted material. It does not execute web page JavaScript.

Limit: URL parameters can also transmit data. Publicly reachable internal services need additional blocking rules; the protection applies to this tool.

Example: read a public product page; its redirect to a private network address is rejected.

Web tool and address check

Original slide 63

set.title: Operations need metrics and deletion routines
set.content:
Backup · Integration · nr-llm v0.43.19

Evaluate usage
View requests, tokens and estimated costs by provider, model and user.

Trace runs
Check metadata on status, steps, model calls and decisions in the run timeline.

Operate retention
Choose storage scope and retention periods. Have the deletion run executed regularly.

Costs are estimates. A deletion period only takes effect through a scheduled deletion run.

Run timeline and limits · Retention and deletion run

Original slide 49

set.title: Which shared AI layer suits the integration?
set.content:
Backup · Shared services with different focuses

FoundationFocusCheck for the selection
Netresearch nr-llmServices, configurations, tasks and toolsSuitable API and rules for your own application
b13 AiM · AlphaAI proxy, routing and rules; Symfony AI bridgesRequired bridges and changes to the alpha API
T3Planet AI FoundationService API, providers, prompts, context and MCPIntegration of your own extension and operating model
LIA Middleware AICentral AI connection for extensions and custom developmentCommercial; clarify API and licence with the vendor
Madj2k AI Core + AI AssistantPHP core and TYPO3 integration for assistance, pipelines and RAGFit with your own search or assistance workflow

Compare on a concrete task: interface, data path, permissions, costs and maintenance.

Original slide 53

set.title: Quality is measured on example tasks
set.content:
Backup · Decision · nr-llm v0.43.19

  1. Define test cases Collect typical tasks, expected statements and reference answers.
  2. Assess answers Check fixed rules; optionally the DecisionGrader assesses via the DecisionService.
  3. Compare runs Pass rate and assessments make regressions visible.

Evaluations run separately. A check within the workflow has to be built in by the application as well.

Example: does the answer contain the documented opening hours and the expected format?

How it works and source evidence

Original slide 40

set.title: An agent works in a bounded loop
set.content:
Backup · Development · nr-llm v0.43.19

  1. Request Assemble goal, configuration, skills and permitted tools.
  2. Model Answers directly or proposes a tool call.
  3. Approval For calls that require approval, pause and wait for the decision.
  4. Tool Execute the permitted call and add the result to the history.
  5. Next round The model receives the result and decides the next step.

The model proposes steps; nr-llm controls execution, pauses and limits.

↶ The tool result goes back to the model's decision – until there is an answer or a limit is reached.

How it works and source evidence

Original slide 43

set.title: Tool access needs several approvals
set.content:
Backup · Integration · nr-llm v0.43.19

  1. Enable the tool Enable the group and the individual tool centrally.
  2. Limit the task Limit groups per configuration and run; exclude individual tools.
  3. Check user permissions Per tool: check admin requirement or specific TYPO3 permissions.
  4. Confirm the change For the built-in writing tools, approve the planned change in advance.

A consent replaces neither user permissions nor tool and data limits.

Data class and provider zone apply in addition: read_source is blocked with externalGlobal + enforce.

Tool permissions in the source code · Write permissions and approvals

Original slide 48

set.title: What is a write approval bound to?
set.content:
Backup · Control and responsibility · nr-llm 0.43.19

A different person
With the four-eyes rule enabled, the triggering backend user may not approve themselves. This also applies to administrators.

Reviewed state
The approval must match the pending calls. A preview that has changed in the meantime requires a new decision.

Stored evidence
Before a write step, the approval event must be stored. If that fails, the approved step is not executed.

Limit: four-eyes applies to backend users. State binding requires a successful tool preview; approval does not replace a review on the merits.

Example: a displayed original value changes during approval. The agent waits again with a new preview.

Four-eyes rule · Preview binding · Call and audit

Original slide 64

set.title: How does the project add custom tool rules?
set.content:
Backup · Control and responsibility · nr-llm 0.43.19

  1. Develop the rule The application implements its own business condition through the interface for tool rules.
  2. Check before execution The rule assesses final arguments, acting user and target. It checks again even after human approval.
  3. Apply the decision A rejecting rule prevents the call. Errors in a rule also lead to rejection.

Limit: without a custom rule there is no additional business check. The rule must explicitly reject required but missing target information.

Project example: this automation may only change records in the approved page area.

Custom tool rules

Original slide 65

set.title: When is a shared AI foundation worth it?
set.content:
Decision · Criteria for a pilot

Recurring work
A concrete task comes up regularly. Content and workflow already live in TYPO3.

Shared control
Several applications need the same providers, models, budgets or approval rules.

Measurable benefit
In the pilot, compare time including rework, result quality and running costs with the previous workflow.

Introduce it when the measured benefit justifies integration and operations.

Compare modules and requirements

Original slide 50

set.title: How do we limit costs?
set.content:
Decision · nr-llm v0.43.19 · checked features

Before the call
nr-llm checks configured user and configuration limits. Planned costs that are passed in are included in the check.

After the call
nr-llm records the reported usage. Estimated costs come from the response or the model prices.

Add in operations
Reconcile prices and the provider's invoice. For a hard cost limit, also plan a reservation or a block.

Parallel calls can exceed the budget. The advance check does not guarantee a hard cost limit.

Budgets and their limits

Original slide 51

set.title: What must be settled before productive use?
set.content:
Decision · Recommendation for introduction

Data flow
Which data goes where? Define provider, region and retention for the model, fallback path and tools.

Permissions and approval
Who may read, write and publish? Name the responsible person and the approval step per workflow.

Quality
Test typical tasks and critical errors. Define in advance which results people must review.

Operations
Assign responsibility for costs, logs and updates. Define shutdown and procedure in case of outage.

Go live once data paths, approvals, quality standard and operational responsibility are settled.

Data flows and responsibility at a glance

Original slide 52

set.title: MCP servers: which access to TYPO3?
set.content:
Backup · Integration · publicly reviewed project sources

hauptsache.net
Standalone server.
Edit records via workspaces; add your own PHP tools.

Marek Skopal
Standalone server.
Direct management as the main mode; workspaces optional and TCA tools extensible.

AutoDudes MCP
Add-on to the AI Suite.
Offers TYPO3 content and selected AI features through the suite's services and permissions.

MCP gives assistants tool access. AI connection, permissions and approvals remain separate decisions.

hauptsache.net · MCP server · Marek Skopal · MCP server
